terms.name: Crankshaft
terms.definition: The main rotating shaft inside the engine. Connecting rods turn the pistons’ up-and-down movement into rotation here.
terms.details: That rotation ultimately drives the transmission and wheels. The crankshaft also drives other engine systems; the external crankshaft pulley is a separate part attached at its front.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Component View.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 10 identifies crankshaft.

terms.name: Piston
terms.definition: A close-fitting moving part inside each engine cylinder. Pressure from combustion pushes it down.
terms.details: The connecting rod passes that force to the crankshaft. Piston rings help seal combustion pressure and control oil along the cylinder wall.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Component View.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies the piston and connecting-rod assembly.

terms.name: Connecting rod
terms.definition: The link between a piston and the crankshaft. It carries combustion force while changing angle as the crankshaft turns.
terms.details: Its bearing allows movement at the crankshaft without metal surfaces simply rubbing together. The correct oil supply and bearing clearances matter.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Component View.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies the piston and connecting-rod assembly.

terms.name: Cylinder block
terms.definition: The main engine casting that contains the cylinders and supports the crankshaft.
terms.details: Oil and coolant passages are built into the block. The cylinder heads bolt onto it; the block and heads are separate components.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Component View.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 4 identifies cylinder block.

terms.name: Cylinder head
terms.definition: The upper engine casting that contains the valves and forms the top of the combustion chambers.
terms.details: It routes incoming air and outgoing exhaust. The head gasket seals the joint between the cylinder head and cylinder block.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 20 identifies the left cylinder head.

terms.name: Camshaft
terms.definition: A rotating shaft with shaped lobes that open the engine’s valves at the right points in its cycle.
terms.details: Intake valves let the fresh charge enter; exhaust valves let burned gases leave. Camshaft timing determines when those events happen.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 11 identifies the left intake camshaft.

terms.name: Valve train
terms.definition: The group of parts that opens and closes the engine’s intake and exhaust valves.
terms.details: The exact mechanism differs by engine. The 3.7L description uses direct-acting mechanical buckets, so instructions for another engine’s followers or lash adjusters are not interchangeable.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

terms.name: Timing chain
terms.definition: A chain inside the engine that keeps crankshaft and camshaft movement synchronized.
terms.details: Its job is valve timing. It is different from the visible accessory belt that powers equipment outside the engine.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies timing chain.

terms.name: Variable camshaft timing
terms.definition: A system that changes camshaft timing while the engine runs, adjusting when valves open or close.
terms.details: Twin independent timing lets intake and exhaust timing be controlled separately. Oil-controlled actuators and control solenoids work with the engine controller to make those changes.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

terms.name: Engine oil pump
terms.definition: The pump that supplies oil to the engine’s lubrication passages.
terms.details: Oil flow lubricates loaded bearings and operates oil-controlled engine components. A relief valve limits pressure by diverting oil; oil pressure and the amount of oil in the sump describe different things.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies engine oil pump.

terms.name: Oil pickup tube
aliases: oil pump screen and pickup tube
terms.definition: The tube and screened inlet through which the oil pump draws oil from the sump.
terms.details: The screen catches larger debris before it reaches the pump. A blocked inlet or loss of sealing can interfere with oil supply even when oil is present in the pan.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 3 identifies oil pickup tube.

terms.name: Oil pan
terms.definition: The lower engine cover that holds the oil reservoir.
terms.details: Oil returns here after circulating through the engine. The drain plug is fitted to the pan, while the oil pump sends oil back through the lubrication system.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 4 identifies oil pan.

terms.name: Oil filter
terms.definition: A filter in the lubrication circuit that captures contamination carried by engine oil.
terms.details: It works alongside the specified oil, not instead of it. Filter design and installation instructions vary by engine, so check the selected engine’s procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01D Engine - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT/General Procedures/Engine Oil Draining and Filling.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 5 identifies oil filter.

terms.name: Crankshaft front seal
terms.definition: The seal that keeps engine oil inside where the front of the crankshaft passes through its surrounding cover.
terms.details: The crankshaft rotates while the seal housing stays still. The sealing surface, installation direction and specified installer matter; a seal replacement is more than pressing a rubber ring into any convenient position.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01C Engine - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT/Removal and Installation/Crankshaft Front Seal.html

mediaRefs.caption: 5.0L front-seal removal view. The seal is highlighted blue; the purple equipment is the specified removal tool.

terms.name: Intake manifold
terms.definition: The assembly that distributes intake air to the engine’s cylinders.
terms.details: The throttle body controls incoming airflow before it is distributed. Manifold shape and connections vary by engine, which is why diagrams must match the selected engine.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies the upper intake manifold.

terms.name: Accessory drive belt
terms.definition: The external belt that transfers engine rotation to belt-driven accessories.
terms.details: Follow the diagram for the actual engine: the route and driven components can differ. The belt is separate from the engine’s internal timing chains.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 2 identifies accessory drive belt. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: Accessory drive belt tensioner
terms.definition: The spring-loaded assembly that keeps the accessory belt under tension as the system operates.
terms.details: Its pulley presses against the belt. The complete tensioner includes the moving arm and spring mechanism; that is different from a fixed idler pulley.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 1 identifies accessory drive belt tensioner. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: Crankshaft belt pulley
terms.definition: The wheel at the front of the crankshaft that drives the accessory belt.
terms.details: It passes engine rotation into the belt system. Read its callout separately from the crankshaft itself and from the pulley on each driven accessory.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 3 identifies crankshaft belt pulley. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: A/C compressor belt
terms.definition: The belt that transmits rotation to the air-conditioning compressor drive.
terms.details: The 3.7L component map identifies this separately from the main accessory belt. Use the illustrated routing and the dedicated removal procedure instead of assuming every belt shares the same tensioning arrangement.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 4 identifies a/c compressor belt. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: A/C compressor pulley
terms.definition: The belt-contact wheel on the air-conditioning compressor drive.
terms.details: The pulley is the visible rotating drive part; the compressor is the larger assembly that circulates refrigerant. A diagram label for the pulley does not mean the whole compressor is being identified or replaced.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 5 identifies a/c compressor pulley. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: Coolant pump pulley
terms.definition: The pulley that transfers belt rotation to the coolant pump.
terms.details: On the 3.7L engine, the accessory belt drives this pulley and therefore the pump. The pulley sits outside the coolant circuit; the pump’s impeller moves coolant inside it.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 6 identifies coolant pump pulley. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: Generator pulley
terms.definition: The belt-contact wheel that turns the generator.
terms.details: The generator converts that mechanical rotation into electrical energy. A pulley concern and an internal electrical generator concern can have different causes even though both affect the same assembly.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-05B Accessory Drive - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Accessory Drive - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L accessory-drive map. Callout 7 identifies generator pulley. These numbers identify parts, not repair steps.

terms.name: Coolant pump
terms.definition: The pump that circulates coolant through the engine and its cooling circuits.
terms.details: Moving coolant carries heat away from the engine. The 3.7L description identifies an accessory-belt-driven pump; do not assume the same drive arrangement for every engine.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L cooling-flow diagram. Callout 3: Coolant pump. The arrows show the original coolant paths.

terms.name: Thermostat
terms.definition: A temperature-operated valve that controls coolant flow through the radiator circuit.
terms.details: It helps the engine warm up and then regulates cooling. On the 3.7L engine it is on the cooler inlet side, so its warm-up behavior differs from a thermostat on the hot outlet side.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L cooling-flow diagram. Callout 5 marks the thermostat housing; the thermostat valve is inside that housing.

terms.name: Radiator
terms.definition: The heat exchanger that transfers heat from engine coolant to outside air.
terms.details: Coolant flows inside its passages while air moves across its fins. It relies on both coolant circulation and airflow; those are two different parts of the cooling system.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L cooling-flow diagram. Callout 8: Radiator. The arrows show the original coolant paths.

terms.name: Degas bottle
terms.definition: The coolant container that provides room for expansion and helps remove air from the cooling system.
terms.details: On the described 3.7L system it is also the service fill point and supplies reserve coolant. It belongs to the pressurized cooling system; follow the cooling safety procedure before opening it.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L cooling-flow diagram. Callout 10: Degas bottle. The arrows show the original coolant paths.

terms.name: Heater core
terms.definition: A small heat exchanger that uses hot engine coolant to warm cabin air.
terms.details: Cabin air passes across it while coolant stays inside its passages. It is part of the coolant circuit even though its job is passenger comfort.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L cooling-flow diagram. Callout 16: Heater core. The arrows show the original coolant paths.

terms.name: Cooling fan
terms.definition: The powered fan that moves air through the cooling heat exchangers.
terms.details: It helps supply airflow when road speed alone is not enough. The control system may command it according to operating conditions, so apparent fan behavior should be checked against the diagnostic procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03D Engine Cooling - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT/Removal and Installation/Cooling Fan Motor and Shroud.html

terms.name: Cylinder head temperature sensor
terms.definition: A sensor that reports cylinder-head temperature to the engine controller.
terms.details: The 3.7L fail-safe cooling strategy uses this information when the engine overheats. A warning is a reason to respond to the temperature concern, not to assume the sensor itself is defective.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-03B Engine Cooling - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Cooling - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Fuel injector
terms.definition: An electrically controlled valve that meters fuel into the engine.
terms.details: Injection layout differs by engine. Port injection delivers fuel upstream of the intake valve, while direct injection delivers it into the cylinder; their pressures and service procedures are not interchangeable.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-04B Fuel Charging and Controls - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Fuel Charging and Controls - Component Location.html

terms.name: Fuel rail
terms.definition: The fuel distribution passage that supplies the injectors.
terms.details: It can retain pressurized fuel after the engine stops. Use the relevant pressure-release procedure before opening the system; the rail’s appearance alone does not tell you whether pressure is gone.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/10: Fuel System - General Information/310-01B Fuel Tank and Lines - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Fuel Tank and Lines - Overview.html

terms.name: Fuel pump
terms.definition: The pump that moves fuel from the tank toward the engine’s fuel delivery system.
terms.details: The 3.7L tank module also contains other functions, including filtration and pressure-control features. The pump and the fuel-level sender have different jobs even when housed together.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/10: Fuel System - General Information/310-01B Fuel Tank and Lines - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Fuel Tank and Lines - Overview.html

terms.name: Fuel level sender
terms.definition: The sensor that reports the fuel level in the tank.
terms.details: It provides a measurement for the fuel gauge. A level-reading problem is different from a pump’s ability to deliver fuel, although both parts may be attached to the same module.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/10: Fuel System - General Information/310-01B Fuel Tank and Lines - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Fuel Tank and Lines - Overview.html

terms.name: Fuel tank pressure sensor
terms.definition: A sensor that measures pressure in the fuel tank vapor system.
terms.details: It helps the control system monitor the vapor system. It is not the same measurement as the liquid fuel pressure at the injectors.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-13B Evaporative Emissions - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Evaporative Emissions - Overview.html

terms.name: Evaporative emissions system
terms.definition: The system that contains fuel vapor and manages its later use by the engine instead of letting it escape freely.
terms.details: The vapor plumbing and its control valves have a different purpose from the liquid fuel supply lines. A vapor-system diagnostic code does not automatically identify a bad fuel pump.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-13B Evaporative Emissions - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Evaporative Emissions - Overview.html

terms.name: Throttle body
terms.definition: The intake assembly containing the valve that controls how much air enters the engine.
terms.details: With electronic throttle control, the engine controller commands the valve using accelerator and other operating information. Pedal movement is a request to the control system, not simply a cable pulling the valve.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-04B Fuel Charging and Controls - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Fuel Charging and Controls - Component Location.html

terms.name: Ignition coil
terms.definition: An electrical transformer that produces the high voltage needed for a spark at the spark plug.
terms.details: In a coil-on-plug arrangement, each coil is positioned at its spark plug. A misfire still needs diagnosis: spark, fuel and the cylinder’s mechanical condition all matter.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 1 identifies ignition coil.

terms.name: Spark plug
terms.definition: The part that provides a controlled spark gap inside the combustion chamber.
terms.details: The ignition coil supplies the voltage; the spark starts combustion of the air-fuel mixture. Use the plug type, gap and installation specification for the exact engine.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-07B Engine Ignition - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Removal and Installation/Spark Plugs.html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 18 identifies spark plug.

terms.name: Powertrain control module
terms.definition: The computer that uses sensor information and stored control strategies to manage engine and powertrain functions.
terms.details: Its inputs describe conditions; its outputs command devices such as actuators and solenoids. A fault code involving a controlled component does not by itself prove the module needs replacement.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-14B Electronic Engine Controls - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Electronic Engine Controls - Overview.html

terms.name: Diagnostic trouble code
terms.definition: A code stored by a control module when its monitoring detects a problem.
terms.details: Think of it as a clue describing the circuit or condition the module noticed. Follow the matching diagnostic path to find the cause instead of treating the code as a parts shopping list.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Parameter identification
terms.definition: A named data value that a scan tool can read from a vehicle module.
terms.details: A PID may show a sensor reading, an output state or a diagnostic status. Some scan tools can also command output functions, but reading codes alone does not provide every test capability.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Diagnostic scan tool
terms.definition: Equipment that communicates with vehicle modules to read faults and operating data or perform supported tests.
terms.details: Check the functions required by the procedure. A basic code reader may not offer network tests, module self-tests, output commands or relearn functions.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Digital multimeter
terms.definition: An instrument for measuring electrical values such as voltage and resistance.
terms.details: Select the right function and connection for the test. Resistance measurements and voltage measurements have different setup requirements; a circuit can show continuity yet still fail under load.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Voltage drop
terms.definition: The voltage used up across part of a circuit while current is flowing.
terms.details: An excessive drop can reveal resistance in a connection or wire that a no-load check misses. The test points and operating load come from the relevant diagnostic procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Ground circuit
terms.definition: The electrical return path that completes a circuit back to the power source.
terms.details: A poor ground can affect several devices sharing that path. Measuring it under load helps distinguish a sound connection from one that merely looks connected.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Connector terminal
terms.definition: The metal contact inside an electrical connector.
terms.details: The plastic housing locates the contacts, but the terminals carry the current. Fit and contact force matter; pushing an oversized probe into a terminal can damage it.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Wiring harness
terms.definition: An organized bundle of wires and connectors that carries power and signals through the vehicle.
terms.details: Routing, clips and protective coverings keep it away from heat, sharp edges and moving parts. A rubbed-through wire can create an intermittent problem that changes with movement.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Generator
terms.definition: The engine-driven electrical machine that powers the vehicle’s electrical system and charges the battery while running.
terms.details: It generates alternating current internally and converts it to direct current. The charging controller regulates its output; the battery and generator work together but perform different jobs.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/14: Battery and Charging System/414-00 Charging System - General Information/Description and Operation/Charging System - Overview.html

terms.name: Voltage regulator
terms.definition: The generator control that adjusts its electrical output toward the requested voltage.
terms.details: The described charging system lets the PCM communicate a voltage setpoint to the regulator. A charging diagnosis therefore involves control signals as well as the generator’s mechanical drive.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/14: Battery and Charging System/414-00 Charging System - General Information/Description and Operation/Charging System - Overview.html

terms.name: Battery state of charge
terms.definition: An estimate of how much usable charge the battery currently holds.
terms.details: A battery can be partly discharged without being permanently defective. The diagnostic methods specify a minimum state of charge before testing because low supply voltage can confuse other results.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 1: General Information/00: Service Information/100-00 General Information/Description and Operation/Diagnostic Methods.html

terms.name: Battery current sensor
terms.definition: The sensor that measures current flowing into or out of the battery.
terms.details: The body control module uses battery information to manage electrical loads. On this system the current sensor is attached to the negative battery cable.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/14: Battery and Charging System/414-00 Charging System - General Information/Description and Operation/Charging System - Overview.html

terms.name: Body control module
terms.definition: The controller that coordinates many body electrical functions and exchanges information with other modules.
terms.details: Its work includes power-management information in the described charging system. Body electronics can depend on messages from elsewhere in the car, so a symptom does not always originate at the device that appears affected.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/14: Battery and Charging System/414-00 Charging System - General Information/Description and Operation/Charging System - Overview.html

terms.name: Controller area network
terms.definition: A communication network that lets vehicle modules share messages over wiring.
terms.details: A module may use information measured by another module rather than having its own sensor. Network faults can therefore affect several systems at once.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/18: Electrical Distribution/418-00 Module Communications Network/Description and Operation/Communications Network - Overview.html

terms.name: Gateway module
terms.definition: The module that relays selected information between the vehicle’s different communication networks.
terms.details: For example, steering-system messages can pass through the gateway on their way to other modules. A network diagram shows these information paths, not a direct wire for every individual signal.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Electronic power assist steering
terms.definition: Steering assistance supplied by an electric motor under electronic control.
terms.details: The driver still turns the steering wheel, while the motor reduces the effort needed. The described system varies assistance with steering torque and vehicle speed.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Power steering control module
terms.definition: The controller that calculates steering assistance and commands the steering-assist motor.
terms.details: It uses torque-sensor information and network messages, monitors faults and may reduce or remove assistance when required by its failure strategy.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

mediaRefs.caption: EPAS system schematic, not a physical-location drawing. Callout 8 represents power steering control module.

terms.name: Steering gear
terms.definition: The assembly that turns steering input into side-to-side movement to steer the front wheels.
terms.details: In this EPAS system the motor, controller and torque sensor are part of the gear assembly. Inner and outer tie rods connect its movement to the wheels.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

mediaRefs.caption: EPAS system schematic, not a physical-location drawing. Callout 1 represents steering gear.

terms.name: Steering torque sensor
terms.definition: The sensor that measures the driver’s twisting effort at the steering input.
terms.details: It detects relative rotation across a torsion bar. That lets the steering controller distinguish a light input from a stronger request for help; it is different from simply measuring steering-wheel angle.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

mediaRefs.caption: EPAS system schematic, not a physical-location drawing. Callout 7 represents steering torque sensor.

terms.name: Tie rod
terms.definition: A link that carries steering-gear movement to the wheel’s steering connection.
terms.details: The inner and outer portions connect the gear to the knuckle while allowing suspension and steering movement. Toe alignment and tie-rod service are related, but a component diagram is not an alignment procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Steering gear bellows boot
terms.definition: The flexible protective cover at each side of the steering gear.
terms.details: Its folds allow the tie rod to move while helping keep contamination away from the protected joint and rack area. The cover and its clamps are separate service parts in the steering description.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/11: Steering System/211-02 Power Steering/Description and Operation/Power Steering - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Coil spring
terms.definition: The suspension spring that supports vehicle load and allows controlled wheel movement over bumps.
terms.details: A spring stores and releases energy as it compresses and expands. The shock absorber controls the resulting motion; the two parts have different jobs.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 1 identifies coil spring.

terms.name: Shock absorber
terms.definition: The suspension component that resists motion to control bouncing and wheel movement.
terms.details: The spring carries the load and stores energy; the damper controls how quickly that movement settles. On the described rear suspension the shock mounts to the lower arm.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 3 identifies shock absorber.

terms.name: Stabilizer bar
terms.definition: The bar that helps resist side-to-side body roll as the suspension moves.
terms.details: Its links connect it to the suspension. It works with the springs and dampers; it is not a replacement for either one.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 2 identifies the stabilizer bar and links.

terms.name: Stabilizer bar link
terms.definition: The short link that transfers suspension movement to the stabilizer bar.
terms.details: It allows the bar to act on the suspension while the joints accommodate movement. A link and the bar itself are separate parts in the component map.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 2 identifies the stabilizer bar and links.

terms.name: Control arm
terms.definition: A suspension link that locates the wheel knuckle relative to the body or subframe while allowing travel.
terms.details: The rear system uses upper and lower arms. Their mounting points and bushings guide movement, so removal and alignment instructions must match the actual arm.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 9 identifies the lower arm and bushing assembly.

terms.name: Suspension bushing
terms.definition: A compliant mounting element between suspension parts.
terms.details: It allows controlled movement while reducing the transfer of vibration. Its position and installed orientation can matter, so use the procedure for the specific joint.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 9 identifies the lower arm and bushing assembly.

terms.name: Toe link
terms.definition: A rear suspension link that helps control the direction the wheel points when viewed from above.
terms.details: That direction is called toe. The link participates in locating the wheel; loosening an adjustment is different from simply identifying it in a diagram.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 8 identifies toe link.

terms.name: Wheel knuckle
terms.definition: The suspension part that carries the wheel hub and connects it to the locating links.
terms.details: At a steering wheel it also turns with steering input. It is a structural mounting part, distinct from the rotating hub and its bearing.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 4 identifies wheel knuckle.

terms.name: Wheel hub
terms.definition: The rotating assembly that supports the mounted wheel and its studs.
terms.details: The wheel bearing lets it rotate while carrying load. Some service procedures treat the hub and bearing as an assembly, so identify the exact part before ordering.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 5 identifies the combined wheel bearing and hub assembly.

terms.name: Wheel bearing
terms.definition: The bearing that lets the wheel hub rotate while supporting vehicle loads.
terms.details: Bearing condition can affect noise and wheel movement. A noise heard near a wheel still needs the prescribed diagnosis because tires and other rotating parts can produce similar symptoms.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Overview.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 5 identifies the combined wheel bearing and hub assembly.

terms.name: Wheel stud
terms.definition: A threaded stud used with a wheel nut to secure the wheel to the hub.
terms.details: The fasteners clamp the wheel to its mounting face. Thread condition and the specified tightening sequence and torque matter; the stud is not a substitute for a sound mounting surface.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-02 Rear Suspension/Description and Operation/Rear Suspension - Component Location.html

mediaRefs.caption: Rear suspension component map. Callout 6 identifies wheel stud.

terms.name: Toe
terms.definition: The direction the wheels point toward or away from each other when viewed from above.
terms.details: It is an alignment measurement. Toe adjustment changes that relationship using the vehicle’s specified adjusters and measured targets.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-00 Suspension System - General Information/General Procedures/Front Toe Adjustment.html

terms.name: Camber
terms.definition: The inward or outward tilt of a wheel when viewed from the front or rear.
terms.details: It is different from road camber, which means the road’s sideways slope. Alignment specifications describe the wheel angle for the selected vehicle setup.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-00 Suspension System - General Information/General Procedures/Rear Camber Adjustment.html

terms.name: Clutch disc
terms.definition: The friction disc that connects a manual-transmission input shaft to engine rotation when clamped by the clutch.
terms.details: Pressing the clutch pedal releases the clamping force so the engine and transmission can turn at different speeds. This definition concerns the manual clutch, not an automatic transmission’s internal clutch packs.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-01 Clutch - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Removal and Installation/Clutch Disc and Pressure Plate - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS).html

terms.name: Clutch pressure plate
terms.definition: The clutch assembly that clamps the friction disc against the flywheel.
terms.details: Its spring force transmits engine torque through the disc. The release mechanism reduces that clamp when you press the pedal.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-01 Clutch - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Removal and Installation/Clutch Disc and Pressure Plate - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS).html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L manual-clutch pressure plate highlighted blue in the removal illustration. The friction disc sits behind it.

terms.name: Flywheel
terms.definition: The rotating part attached to the engine crankshaft that provides the manual clutch’s engine-side friction surface.
terms.details: It also stores rotational energy to smooth changes in engine speed. Surface condition and the exact flywheel design matter to clutch operation.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01B Engine - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS)/Description and Operation/Engine Component View.html

3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-01 Clutch - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Removal and Installation/Clutch Disc and Pressure Plate - 3.7L Duratec (227kW-301PS).html

mediaRefs.caption: 3.7L engine component view. Callout 12 identifies flywheel.

terms.name: Clutch master cylinder
terms.definition: The hydraulic cylinder that turns clutch-pedal movement into fluid pressure.
terms.details: That pressure operates the release side of the clutch system. Air or a leak can change pedal feel and release travel even when the friction disc itself is sound.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-02 Clutch Controls - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Description and Operation/Clutch Controls - Component Location.html

terms.name: Clutch slave cylinder
terms.definition: The hydraulic actuator that uses clutch fluid pressure to operate the release mechanism.
terms.details: The release bearing transfers that movement to the rotating clutch assembly. Cylinder and bearing arrangements vary, so follow the selected transmission’s service instructions.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-02 Clutch Controls - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Description and Operation/Clutch Controls - Component Location.html

terms.name: Synchronizer
terms.definition: The mechanism that brings rotating transmission parts to compatible speeds before a selected gear engages.
terms.details: It helps a manual gearbox shift smoothly. The MT82 uses different synchronizer arrangements by gear; forcing a reluctant shift does not diagnose which part is at fault.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-03A Manual Transmission - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Description and Operation/Manual Transmission - Overview.html

terms.name: Transmission input shaft
terms.definition: The shaft that receives engine rotation into the transmission.
terms.details: In a manual transmission it is driven through the clutch. The output shaft carries the selected gear’s resulting rotation toward the driveline.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/08: Manual Transmission, Clutch, Transfer Case and Power Transfer Unit/308-03A Manual Transmission - 6-Speed Manual Transmission - MT82/Description and Operation/Manual Transmission - Overview.html

terms.name: Torque converter
terms.definition: The fluid coupling between the engine and automatic transmission.
terms.details: It allows the engine to keep running while the vehicle is stopped in gear and transfers torque as operating conditions change. Its lockup clutch is a separate operating feature, not the driver-operated clutch of a manual car.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/07: Automatic Transmission/307-01 Automatic Transmission - 6-Speed Automatic Transmission - 6R80/Description and Operation/Torque Converter.html

terms.name: Driveshaft
terms.definition: The rotating shaft that carries transmission output to the rear differential.
terms.details: Its joints allow the connected assemblies to sit at working angles. Balance and alignment concerns must be checked as a system rather than blamed on the shaft by sound alone.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html
2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-01 Driveshaft/Diagnosis and Testing/Driveshaft.html

terms.name: Differential
terms.definition: The gear assembly that sends drive to both rear wheels while allowing them to turn at different speeds in a corner.
terms.details: The driveshaft turns the pinion, which drives the ring gear and differential case. The halfshafts carry the resulting torque to the wheels.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html

terms.name: Ring gear
terms.definition: The large gear in the final drive that meshes with the drive pinion.
terms.details: It is attached to the differential case. Gear mesh depends on specified backlash and bearing adjustments, so replacing parts requires more than matching their apparent size.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html

terms.name: Drive pinion
terms.definition: The input gear that receives driveshaft rotation and turns the differential ring gear.
terms.details: Its bearings locate it precisely. Bearing preload and gear-contact setup are separate measurements and require the specified procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html

terms.name: Halfshaft
terms.definition: A shaft that connects one side of the differential to its driven wheel.
terms.details: It must transmit torque while the suspension moves. Its constant-velocity joints accommodate the changing angle and distance.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-05 Rear Drive Halfshafts/Diagnosis and Testing/Rear Drive Halfshafts.html
2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-05 Rear Drive Halfshafts/Removal and Installation/Rear Halfshaft.html

terms.name: Constant velocity joint
terms.definition: A driveline joint designed to transmit rotation smoothly through a changing angle.
terms.details: The protective boot keeps grease in and contamination out. A damaged boot and a worn joint are different findings, even though one can eventually lead to the other.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-05 Rear Drive Halfshafts/Diagnosis and Testing/Rear Drive Halfshafts.html
2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-05 Rear Drive Halfshafts/Removal and Installation/Rear Halfshaft.html

terms.name: Brake pad
terms.definition: The replaceable friction material that the caliper presses against the brake disc.
terms.details: Friction slows the wheel and produces heat. Pad wear and disc condition belong in the same inspection, but the service parts and procedure depend on the fitted brake package.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-03 Front Disc Brake/Removal and Installation/Brake Pads - Vehicles With: 2-Piston Brake Caliper.html

mediaRefs.caption: Front 2-piston brake arrangement with the pads highlighted blue. This is a removal illustration, not a wear-limit diagram.

terms.name: Brake disc
terms.definition: The rotating friction surface clamped by the brake pads.
terms.details: It turns with the wheel. Thickness, runout and surface condition are different checks, each with its own specified limits and method.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-03 Front Disc Brake/Removal and Installation/Brake Pads - Vehicles With: 2-Piston Brake Caliper.html

terms.name: Brake caliper
terms.definition: The brake assembly that uses hydraulic piston force to press pads against the disc.
terms.details: Different Mustang brake packages use different caliper designs and piston counts. The correct pad replacement instructions are identified by the caliper fitted to the vehicle.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-03 Front Disc Brake/Removal and Installation/Brake Pads - Vehicles With: 2-Piston Brake Caliper.html

mediaRefs.caption: Front 2-piston caliper positioned aside and supported. Yellow indicates the part moved aside; the hose must not carry its weight.

terms.name: Brake master cylinder
terms.definition: The hydraulic cylinder that converts brake-pedal input into pressure in the brake circuits.
terms.details: That pressure travels through brake fluid to the wheel brakes. It is distinct from the booster, which helps reduce the effort needed at the pedal.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-06 Hydraulic Brake Actuation/Removal and Installation/Brake Master Cylinder.html

terms.name: Brake booster
terms.definition: The device that adds assistance to the driver’s braking effort.
terms.details: The described system uses vacuum assistance and can supplement it through ABS hydraulic control under specified conditions. Assistance and hydraulic pressure generation are related but separate functions.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - Overview.html

terms.name: Anti-lock braking system
terms.definition: The system that helps prevent wheels locking during braking by controlling hydraulic pressure.
terms.details: Keeping the wheels rotating helps preserve steering control. Pump noise and pedal pulsation can occur during active ABS intervention, but persistent concerns still need the appropriate diagnosis.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - Overview.html

terms.name: Hydraulic control unit
terms.definition: The brake hydraulic assembly whose valves and pump adjust pressure for ABS and stability functions.
terms.details: It works with the electronic controller. Opening or replacing hydraulic components can require a specific bleeding procedure, sometimes with scan-tool functions.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - Overview.html

terms.name: Wheel speed sensor
terms.definition: The sensor that reports how quickly a wheel is rotating.
terms.details: ABS and stability control compare wheel-speed information with other inputs. A wheel-speed fault can involve wiring or the signal target as well as the sensor.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Electronic stability control
terms.definition: The system that helps control a developing skid using brake intervention and engine-torque control.
terms.details: It compares the vehicle’s motion with steering and other inputs. It shares hardware with ABS but has a different purpose from simply preventing wheel lock during braking.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - Overview.html

terms.name: Traction control
terms.definition: The system that helps limit drive-wheel spin during acceleration.
terms.details: It coordinates engine and brake control as needed. Traction control addresses acceleration grip; ABS addresses wheel lock during braking.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/06: Brake System/206-09 Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control/Description and Operation/Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control - Overview.html

terms.name: A/C compressor
terms.definition: The compressor that circulates refrigerant through the air-conditioning system.
terms.details: Its mechanical drive is separate from the refrigerant circuit it operates. Refrigerant service requires the correct recovery and charging equipment, not simply loosening a hose.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - System Operation and Component Description.html

4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - Component Location.html

terms.name: Condenser
terms.definition: The heat exchanger where hot refrigerant releases heat to outside air.
terms.details: It works on the refrigerant side of climate control. It is different from the engine radiator even though both rely on airflow at the front of the vehicle.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - System Operation and Component Description.html

4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - Component Location.html

terms.name: Evaporator
terms.definition: The cabin-side heat exchanger that absorbs heat as refrigerant evaporates.
terms.details: Air passing over it is cooled and dried. Moisture removed from that air becomes condensate, which leaves through the drain.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - System Operation and Component Description.html

4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - Component Location.html

terms.name: Blower motor
terms.definition: The electric motor that moves air through the cabin heating and air-conditioning unit.
terms.details: The blower controls airflow; heating and cooling depend on other components. Little air from the vents and air at the wrong temperature are different starting symptoms.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - System Operation and Component Description.html

4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - Component Location.html

terms.name: Blend door
terms.definition: The internal air door used to change how much air passes through the heating path.
terms.details: Its actuator positions the door according to the temperature request. A temperature-control concern can involve air-door movement as well as coolant or refrigerant performance.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - System Operation and Component Description.html

4: Electrical/12: Climate Control System/412-00 Climate Control System - General Information/Description and Operation/Climate Control System - Vehicles With: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) - Component Location.html

terms.name: Weatherstrip
terms.definition: The flexible seal around an opening such as a door or window.
terms.details: It helps keep water, wind and noise out while allowing the opening to move. Correct fit and surface contact matter; a leak does not always mean the rubber alone is damaged.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-00 Body System - General Information/Description and Operation/Body - Overview.html

terms.name: Subframe
terms.definition: A structural assembly bolted to the body that provides mounting points for major mechanical components.
terms.details: The front subframe carries suspension, steering and engine mounting functions; the rear supports the rear suspension. Its position affects the parts attached to it.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/02: Frame and Mounting/502-00 Uni-Body, Subframe and Mounting System/Description and Operation/Frame Assembly - Overview.html

terms.name: Seam sealer
terms.definition: Material used to seal body-panel joints against water and noise paths.
terms.details: It is different from a structural adhesive or a gasket used inside a mechanical assembly. Choose the specified material for the location and repair.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-00 Body System - General Information/Description and Operation/Body - Overview.html

terms.name: Supplemental restraint system
terms.definition: The coordinated airbag and pretensioner system that supplements the seat belts.
terms.details: Sensors and the restraints controller decide whether deployment is needed. These are safety-critical electrical and pyrotechnic components, so follow the dedicated depowering and handling procedures.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-20B Supplemental Restraint System/Description and Operation/Airbag and Seatbelt Pretensioner Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) - Overview.html

terms.name: Restraints control module
terms.definition: The controller that monitors restraint-system inputs and commands the appropriate deployment when required.
terms.details: Its decision depends on sensor and occupant information. A restraint warning indicates a fault requiring the prescribed diagnostic method, not an invitation to probe deployment circuits arbitrarily.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-20B Supplemental Restraint System/Description and Operation/Airbag and Seatbelt Pretensioner Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) - Overview.html

terms.name: Seatbelt pretensioner
terms.definition: A restraint device that tightens a belt during a qualifying event.
terms.details: It works with the rest of the restraint system to manage occupant movement. It is a deployable component with specific handling and replacement instructions.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-20B Supplemental Restraint System/Description and Operation/Airbag and Seatbelt Pretensioner Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) - Overview.html

terms.name: Connector position assurance
terms.definition: The secondary locking feature that keeps an electrical connector properly secured.
terms.details: On the described deployable restraint connectors, seating this tab also changes the shorting-bar arrangement. A connector can appear attached yet still register a fault if the assurance tab is not fully seated.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 5: Body and Paint/01: Body and Paint/501-20B Supplemental Restraint System/Description and Operation/Airbag and Seatbelt Pretensioner Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) - Overview.html

terms.name: Woodruff key
terms.definition: A small locating key that fits between a shaft and the matching slot in the part mounted on it.
terms.details: At the front crankshaft pulley, the key and slot establish the pulley’s rotational position. The key slot is also a specified sealant location in the 5.0L front-seal procedure; locating the pulley and sealing that path are different jobs.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01C Engine - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT/Removal and Installation/Crankshaft Front Seal.html

mediaRefs.caption: 5.0L crankshaft pulley: the close-up points to the Woodruff key slot, where this procedure specifies sealant.

terms.name: O-ring seal
terms.definition: A flexible ring that seals a joint when compressed in its intended groove or seating area.
terms.details: The ring’s location and size matter. The 5.2L cartridge-filter procedure identifies which new seals to use and specifically leaves out the smallest supplied ring. A ring included in a kit is not automatically correct for every application.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01D Engine - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT/General Procedures/Engine Oil Draining and Filling.html

mediaRefs.caption: 5.2L cartridge-filter illustration: the ring seals are shown separately from the cartridge and housing. Use the source procedure to identify the seals required for this application.

terms.name: Torque-and-angle tightening
terms.definition: A tightening method that uses a stated torque followed by a measured amount of further rotation.
terms.details: Torque measures turning effort; angle measures rotation. Follow the full sequence, including any deliberate loosening stage. An angle instruction alone does not tell you whether a bolt is reusable—the individual procedure supplies that decision.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01C Engine - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT/Removal and Installation/Crankshaft Front Seal.html

terms.name: Gear backlash
terms.definition: The clearance between mating gear teeth, measured as free movement before the opposite tooth faces contact.
terms.details: In a differential, ring-gear backlash and bearing preload are separate setup measurements. The specified adjustment positions the gear assembly; simply making the gears feel tight does not establish correct mesh.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html
2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/General Procedures/Ring Gear Backlash Adjustment.html
3: Powertrain/03: Engine/303-01A Engine - 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW-314PS)/General Procedures/Balance Shaft Backlash.html

terms.name: Bearing preload
terms.definition: The initial load applied to a bearing arrangement when its parts are assembled and adjusted.
terms.details: Preload controls the bearing’s operating relationship even before external load is applied. The differential uses specific spacers or shims for its different bearings. Use the measurement and adjustment method for that bearing instead of treating preload as a generic fastener torque.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/05: Driveline/205-02 Rear Drive Axle-Differential/Description and Operation/Rear Drive Axle and Differential - Overview.html

terms.name: Suspension strut
terms.definition: A suspension assembly that provides damping and also serves as a structural locating member for the wheel.
terms.details: In this front suspension, a coil spring surrounds the strut. The assembly supports vehicle weight and provides the upper pivot relationship for steering, while the lower arms and ball joints locate the lower end. It therefore does more than a separately mounted shock absorber.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-01 Front Suspension/Description and Operation/Front Suspension.html

terms.name: Ball joint
terms.definition: A pivoting joint that connects suspension parts while allowing angular movement.
terms.details: The front suspension’s lower arms use ball joints at the lower steering pivot points. Their ability to move and their ability to locate the wheel securely are both important; use the specified inspection for the particular joint.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-01 Front Suspension/Description and Operation/Front Suspension.html

terms.name: Suspension height sensor
terms.definition: A sensor that reports suspension position to the dynamic-suspension controller.
terms.details: In the described adaptive system, its changing voltage provides position information. The vehicle dynamics module combines this with vehicle-motion messages to decide how much damping each corner needs. Sensor replacement or disturbance can require the system’s specified calibration procedure.

sourceRefs.documentPath: 2: Chassis/04: Suspension/204-05 Vehicle Dynamic Suspension/Description and Operation/Vehicle Dynamic Suspension - System Operation and Component Description.html

terms.name: Vehicle dynamics control module
terms.definition: The controller that adjusts the dampers on vehicles equipped with the described dynamic-suspension system.
terms.details: It combines height-sensor information with network data about braking, cornering and vehicle motion, then controls the damper coils individually. This is an equipment-specific system; a conventional suspension does not gain these functions simply because it has struts and shocks.

terms.name: Tire pressure monitoring system
terms.definition: The system that uses wheel-mounted sensors to monitor tire pressure and warn about low pressure or a system fault.
terms.details: The battery-powered sensors transmit by radio to the radio transceiver module. That module passes the information to the body control module, which manages TPMS operation. Low-pressure and malfunction indications have different meanings; the system description explains how to distinguish them.

terms.name: Radio transceiver module
terms.definition: The radio communication module that receives the tire-pressure sensors’ transmitted data in the TPMS system.
terms.details: It passes that pressure information to the body control module over a local communication link. The sensor, the receiver and their communication path are separate parts of the diagnosis, so failure to receive a reading does not automatically prove the wheel sensor is bad.

terms.name: Thermostatic expansion valve
terms.definition: The refrigerant-metering valve at the evaporator that separates the high-pressure and low-pressure sides of the A/C circuit.
terms.details: Its internal temperature-sensing element responds to refrigerant leaving the evaporator and adjusts how much refrigerant enters it. Think of it as the evaporator’s adjustable feed valve: it regulates refrigerant flow, while the cabin temperature door controls airflow through the heater.

terms.name: Receiver drier
terms.definition: A refrigerant reservoir and moisture-removal component on the high-pressure side of the air-conditioning system.
terms.details: Liquid refrigerant is held ready for the evaporator, and a desiccant inside captures moisture. The manual places the receiver drier alongside the condenser. It works on refrigerant inside the sealed circuit; it does not filter the air you breathe in the cabin.

terms.name: A/C pressure transducer
terms.definition: The sensor that reports refrigerant discharge pressure to the engine controller.
terms.details: The powertrain control module uses this information when deciding whether compressor operation is allowed. A pressure reading describes an operating condition; it does not measure the quantity of refrigerant directly. That distinction matters when following a diagnosis instead of assuming every cooling problem means the system needs more refrigerant.

terms.name: Cabin air filter
terms.definition: The filter that catches particles in the airflow used by the passenger-compartment ventilation system.
terms.details: It belongs to the cabin’s air path, separate from the engine air cleaner. The linked removal procedure reaches it through the lower passenger-side instrument panel area. When following an airflow complaint, distinguishing the cabin filter from the blower motor and its controls helps you understand which part filters air and which part moves it.

terms.name: Air inlet door
terms.definition: The HVAC flap that selects outside air or recirculated cabin air.
terms.details: A small reversible actuator moves the door, and a position sensor tells the climate controller where it is. Recirculation changes where the air comes from; it does not by itself create cooling. The blower still moves the air, and the evaporator and heater core change its temperature.

terms.name: Air distribution door
terms.definition: The flap that directs conditioned air toward the dashboard vents, floor outlets or defrost outlets.
terms.details: Its actuator changes the air’s destination. This is a different job from the temperature blend door, which changes how much air is heated. The manual describes position feedback so the climate controller can compare the requested door position with where the actuator has moved.

terms.name: Evaporator temperature sensor
terms.definition: The temperature sensor used to monitor cooling at the evaporator and help keep it from icing.
terms.details: The sensor is a thermistor: its electrical resistance changes with temperature. The climate controls pass the temperature information to the engine controller, which can stop compressor operation when it becomes too cold. The sensor reports temperature; it does not open or close the refrigerant flow itself.

terms.name: Blower motor speed control
terms.definition: The electronic controller that changes the cabin blower’s speed.
terms.details: It receives a pulse-width-modulated command from the climate controller and varies the blower’s electrical ground feed. In plain terms, the climate controls request an airflow level and this component adjusts the motor’s electrical drive. It is separate from the motor that actually turns the fan.

terms.name: EVAP canister
terms.definition: The storage component that captures fuel vapor instead of letting it escape directly into the air.
terms.details: Activated carbon holds vapor from the fuel tank. During a purge cycle, the stored vapor is drawn into the engine to be burned, leaving the carbon ready to capture more. The canister, purge valve and vent valve have different jobs, so a reference to the canister does not mean either valve.

terms.name: EVAP purge valve
terms.definition: The electrically controlled valve that regulates fuel-vapor flow from the EVAP canister toward the engine intake.
terms.details: Purging empties stored vapor from the canister so the engine can consume it. The purge valve meters that route. The vent valve handles the canister’s outside-air route instead; their similar names do not make them interchangeable. Follow the engine-specific diagram to identify the correct valve and hose connections.

terms.name: EVAP canister vent solenoid
terms.definition: The electrically operated valve controlling the EVAP canister’s connection to outside air.
terms.details: The fresh-air path and its filter serve a different purpose from the purge hose leading to the intake. This is why the manual lists the vent solenoid separately from the purge valve. A diagnosis needs to distinguish these routes rather than treating every EVAP valve as the same part.

terms.name: High-pressure fuel pump
terms.definition: The pump that raises fuel pressure for the engine’s direct-injection circuit.
terms.details: In the manual’s EcoBoost layout, it is separate from the fuel-supply pump in the tank and from the high-pressure pump drive unit. The pump feeds the rail; the injectors then meter fuel into the cylinders. Identifying which side of the fuel system is being discussed matters because the pressure-release and line-handling procedures differ.

terms.name: Positive crankcase ventilation valve
terms.definition: The valve that regulates crankcase-vapor flow into the engine’s intake system.
terms.details: Some combustion gases pass the piston rings and enter the crankcase; this is called blow-by. Ventilation carries those gases away so pressure and contamination do not simply build up inside. The PCV valve controls that flow, while the connecting hoses and any oil separator serve related but distinct roles.

terms.name: Turbocharger
terms.definition: An exhaust-driven air compressor that helps the engine take in a greater mass of air.
terms.details: Exhaust turns a turbine wheel connected by a shaft to the compressor wheel. The compressor pressurizes incoming air; it does not mix exhaust directly into that fresh-air passage. The manual’s turbocharger references are for the EcoBoost engine, so their hardware layout does not apply to the naturally aspirated engines.

terms.name: Charge air cooler
terms.definition: The heat exchanger that cools air after the turbocharger has compressed it.
terms.details: Compression heats the intake air. Cooling it makes the air denser before it reaches the cylinders. The charge air cooler and its pipes carry intake air, unlike the engine radiator, which carries coolant. The linked Mustang component and pipe procedures belong to the EcoBoost intake system.

terms.name: Turbocharger wastegate
terms.definition: The exhaust bypass valve used to regulate how much energy drives the turbocharger turbine.
terms.details: Allowing some exhaust to bypass the turbine reduces the energy available to spin the compressor. That helps control boost. This is different from an intake-side bypass valve, which works on compressed fresh air. The manual’s turbocharger diagram identifies the wastegate-related hardware for the EcoBoost engine.

terms.name: Transmission valve body
terms.definition: The automatic transmission’s hydraulic control assembly, which routes and regulates fluid pressure.
terms.details: Internal passages and valves direct fluid to the transmission’s working elements. Electrically commanded solenoids help the engine controller manage engagement and shift feel. The valve body is therefore where electrical commands are turned into hydraulic action; it is not the transmission’s gearset.

terms.name: Transmission solenoid
terms.definition: An electrically controlled valve used to control fluid flow or pressure in the automatic transmission.
terms.details: The controller commands different solenoids for tasks such as selecting hydraulic circuits and controlling line pressure or converter-clutch operation. They do not all behave identically. The manual’s solenoid operation chart is the place to check which named solenoid is active in a particular operating state.

terms.name: Planetary gearset
terms.definition: A group of gears arranged around a central sun gear, with planet gears carried inside an outer ring gear.
terms.details: Different ratios result when different members are driven, held or used as the output. The automatic transmission combines gearsets with clutches to choose those relationships. The ring gear in this assembly belongs to the transmission; it is a different component from the differential ring gear at the rear axle.

terms.name: One-way clutch
terms.definition: A clutch that holds in one direction of rotation and freewheels in the other.
terms.details: The automatic transmission’s low one-way clutch holds the rear planetary carrier in one direction. Allowing motion in the opposite direction changes how torque can return through the gearset during coasting. This directional holding action is different from the pedal-operated clutch used with a manual transmission.

terms.name: Torque converter clutch
terms.definition: The controlled clutch inside the torque-converter system that reduces the slip of the fluid coupling when applied.
terms.details: The source describes separate hydraulic routes for released and applied operation. A dedicated solenoid moves the controlling valves so fluid pressure can apply the clutch. The torque converter can transmit drive while this clutch is released, so converter operation and converter-clutch operation are not the same thing.

terms.name: Transmission fluid pump
terms.definition: The pump that supplies hydraulic pressure to the automatic transmission.
terms.details: In the transmission described here, the torque converter hub drives the pump’s inner gear. The pump draws fluid from the pan through the filter and sends it into the hydraulic system. It supports transmission operation; it is separate from the engine oil pump, despite the shared idea of moving lubricating fluid.

terms.name: Instrument panel cluster
terms.definition: The driver-facing assembly that presents gauges, warning indicators, messages and other vehicle information.
terms.details: The cluster combines information from several systems so you can see vehicle conditions in one place. Its message center also provides settings for supported features. A warning shown in the cluster can originate from another module, so the display location alone does not identify the component that caused it.

terms.definition: The module behind the SYNC system’s connected-device, voice and media functions.
terms.details: It handles inputs such as the microphone, USB devices and Bluetooth audio, and works with the vehicle’s audio and display components. Those pieces are separate modules with separate roles. terms.definition: A local data link used for communication between a controller and nearby electronic devices.
terms.details: LIN carries messages rather than acting as a simple on/off power wire. In the manual, examples include grille-shutter commands and communication from the window switch to the door module on vehicles with a memory seat. A module can therefore need both working power connections and working communication before a feature responds.

terms.definition: An electrically controlled switch that lets a control circuit operate another electrical circuit.
terms.details: In a conventional electromagnetic relay, current through a coil moves contacts that switch the load. This allows a module or small switch to command a higher-current device. Some relays in the Mustang are integrated into modules, so a relay label in a diagram does not guarantee a separate plug-in part.

terms.definition: The mechanism that supports and moves the window glass inside the door.
terms.details: The regulator motor provides motion and the regulator mechanism translates that motion into glass travel. terms.name: Door latch
terms.definition: The mechanism at the door’s closing edge that keeps the door secured when shut.
terms.details: The latch assembly also participates in the locking system.
