terms.definition: The small automatic window movement that helps the frameless door glass clear its weatherstrip.
terms.details: When a door opens, the window motor lowers the glass slightly. After the door closes, it raises the glass back into the weatherstrip channel. The manual describes this function on both coupe and convertible models; it is different from fully lowering a window with the switch.

terms.definition: A set of movable blinds that changes how open the grille’s airflow passage is.
terms.details: An actuator moves one shutter, and linked shutters move with it. The engine controller requests a position using inputs such as coolant temperature, vehicle speed and A/C pressure. The assembly also checks its movement between end positions. It is an actively controlled part, so its resting position alone is not a diagnosis.

terms.name: Steering column
terms.definition: The mechanical connection that carries your steering-wheel rotation toward the steering gear.
terms.details: The steering wheel turns a shaft supported by bearings inside the column. Upper and lower shaft sections and a coupling continue that connection to the gear. This is the physical steering path; the switches and electronic modules mounted nearby have separate jobs. The manual identifies the lower shaft as collapsible and requires a measurement whenever it is disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling.

terms.definition: The electronic interface that connects switches on and around the steering wheel with the vehicle functions they operate.
terms.details: The column stalks and steering-wheel switches connect through this assembly. The manual describes network communication as well as separate circuits for particular functions, so every wire at its connector does not do the same job. terms.definition: The module that locks or unlocks the steering column as part of the vehicle’s theft-deterrent system, where fitted.

The lock module monitors the lock’s position and reports detected faults. terms.name: Cylinder leak-down test
terms.definition: A test that feeds regulated compressed air into a cylinder and measures how much escapes while its valves should be closed.
terms.details: It helps locate a sealing problem after a low compression reading. The path of escaping air can point toward an intake valve, exhaust valve, piston rings, or a leak between cylinders or into the cooling system. The piston position, tester setup, and result limits must follow the engine test procedure; this is different from measuring compression while the starter turns the engine.

terms.name: Fuel trim
terms.definition: The engine computer’s adjustment to fuel delivery to correct the air–fuel mixture using sensor feedback.
terms.details: Short-term trim is the ongoing correction during closed-loop operation. Long-term trim stores corrections learned over time. Read the values under the operating conditions specified by the diagnostic procedure; a correction is a clue to investigate, not proof that a particular sensor or part has failed.

terms.name: Adaptive learning
terms.definition: A control module’s process of learning operating corrections or reference values for the system it controls.
terms.details: The required learning process depends on the module and repair. For example, the 6R80 has a specified drive cycle to restore shift adaptation, while other modules can require a different calibration or learning routine. Follow the matching procedure: learning, programming software, and replacing a failed mechanical part are different jobs.

terms.name: Head gasket
terms.definition: The sealing layer between a cylinder head and the engine block.
terms.details: It helps keep combustion pressure, coolant and oil in their separate passages. Replacing it requires a sound head and block surface, correct fasteners and accurate valve timing; the gasket cannot repair a cracked or distorted casting.

terms.name: Torque-to-yield bolt
terms.definition: A fastener tightened by a specified torque-and-angle process to establish its designed clamping load.
terms.details: The 3.7L Mustang head procedure requires new cylinder-head bolts. Reusing them changes the assumptions behind the tightening process. Follow each separate stage and use the correct fasteners; an aftermarket stud kit is a different installation.

terms.name: Valve tappet
terms.definition: The part between a camshaft lobe and a valve that transfers cam motion while providing the specified clearance.
terms.details: In this 3.7L procedure, reusable tappets return to their original locations. Valve clearance is checked and, when needed, adjusted by selecting the correct tappet thickness rather than randomly swapping them.

terms.name: Torque angle
terms.definition: The measured additional turn of a fastener after a specified tightening stage.
terms.details: A 90-degree stage adds a quarter-turn; it is not a torque-wrench reading. Use an angle gauge and follow the sequence for that fastener. Separate passes through a set of bolts must stay separate.

terms.name: Block deck
terms.definition: The machined top face of the cylinder block where the head gasket sits.
terms.details: Its flatness and condition matter to the seal. Protect it from scratches and debris. Use the application-specific inspection limits; the head and block do not automatically have the same tolerance.
